candidates.definition: Null-corrected self-ablation sensitivity per model (refusal-direction ablation drop, z-scored against random-direction ablations).

nearest_hits.title: Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration
nearest_hits.quote: ablation attacks rely on contrastive estimators to find the refusal direction ... the decoy corrupts their estimator, tricking them into ablating a harmless orthogonal feature while the actual safety mechanism remains intact
nearest_hits.which_properties_match: none scored by benchmark; adversarial caveat on P2 (parent-free): shows the DIM refusal-direction estimator underlying self-ablation sensitivity can be deliberately decoyed post hoc across six model families, so a 'gameable' self-ablation z-score is not a defense-proof safety read. Does not itself compute a per-model scalar correlated with benchmark safety (fails P1+P3 as stated).

nearest_hits.title: Steering Interference Reflects the Model's Defaults, Not the Behavior Directions (v2)
nearest_hits.quote: a direction carrying no behavioral content, matched to a real steer only in the size of the vector it adds, moves the same behaviors in the same order as real steers do
nearest_hits.which_properties_match: Motivates the null/random-direction correction itself (methodology overlap) but is about additive steering, not subtractive ablation, and reports no per-model scalar correlated with a safety benchmark (fails P1, P3). Confirms the random/content-matched control is necessary and non-trivial to interpret, which is exactly what C2n's z-scoring is meant to fix -- not a scoop.

nearest_hits.title: Safety Beyond the Interface: Detecting Harm via Latent States in Large Language Models
nearest_hits.quote: We extract activations from LLaMA-3.1-8B and train lightweight MLP classifier probes (12.6M parameters) to detect harmful prompts. Evaluated on WildJailbreak, Beavertails, and AEGIS 2.0, our probes achieve F1 scores of 99%, 83%, and 84%, respectively
nearest_hits.which_properties_match: The trained artifact is per-PROMPT (classifies whether a given input is harmful), not a per-MODEL scalar (fails P1); single model (LLaMA-3.1-8B) only, no cross-family comparison (fails P4); F1 is against ground-truth prompt labels, not an external per-model safety benchmark score (fails P3).

nearest_hits.title: Local Sparsity Enables Unsupervised LLM Safety Detection
nearest_hits.quote: we propose a framework for locally masked SAE-based anomaly detection, supported by theoretical justifications. We validate it on various architectures and datasets, including both capability-testing datasets and safety-specific datasets
nearest_hits.which_properties_match: Multiple architectures tested (P4-adjacent) but the detector output is per-INPUT anomaly flagging (fails P1, per-model scalar); no learned meta-model pooling hidden stats into one number per model, and no correlation with an external safety benchmark score (fails P3).
